title: Bisimplicial diagonals compute geometric realizations in spaces
statement:
Use simplicial sets, nerves, spaces and coherent colimits as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], the Kan model structure of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper], and the coherent localization $q:\mathsf{sSet}\to\mathcal S$ of [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization]. Let $Z:\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathsf{sSet}$ be any small simplicial diagram of simplicial sets. Its diagonal is $(\operatorname{diag}Z)_n=Z_n{}_n$, with every simplicial operator applied in both variables. There is a natural equivalence
$$\operatorname{colim}_{N(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}})}q(Z_n)\simeq q(\operatorname{diag}Z).$$
It identifies the colimit cocone with the coherent cocone furnished by the simplicial coend $\int^{[n]\in\Delta} Z_n\times\Delta^n\cong\operatorname{diag}Z$. Here the coend in simplicial degree $r$ is the quotient of $\coprod_{n\geq0}(Z_n)_r\times\operatorname{Hom}_\Delta([r],[n])$ by $((Z(\alpha))_r z,t)\sim(z,\alpha\circ t)$ for $\alpha:[m]\to[n]$, $z\in(Z_n)_r$ and $t:[r]\to[m]$. In particular the map from $q(Z_0)$ is induced by $Z_0\times\Delta^0\to\operatorname{diag}Z$. Naturality is with respect to all maps of bisimplicial sets and includes these cocones. No Kan condition on the rows and no extra cofibrancy hypothesis are imposed.

source.place: Example A.2.9.21, Example A.2.9.29, Corollary A.2.9.30 and Example A.2.9.31, printed pp. 844, 849-850; Proposition 4.2.4.4 and Theorem 4.2.4.1 identify model homotopy-colimit cocones with coherent colimit cocones. Read online, not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this result.

proof.text: Put $D(Z)=\int^{[n]}Z_n\times\Delta^n$. Compute this coend degree by degree using exactly the relation in the statement. Define $\phi_r([z,t])=(Z(t))_r(z)\in (Z_r)_r$ for $t:[r]\to[n]$. Functoriality makes $\phi_r$ respect the relation: both representatives of a generating relation map to $(Z(t))_r(Z(\alpha))_r z=(Z(\alpha t))_r z$. Its inverse sends $x\in (Z_r)_r$ to $[x,1_{[r]}]$; the relation with $\alpha=t$ identifies $[z,t]$ with $[(Z(t))_r z,1_{[r]}]$. These bijections respect every inner operator because the two directions of $Z$ commute, and applying an outer operator simultaneously gives exactly the diagonal operator. They are natural in $Z$. Thus $D=\operatorname{diag}$ canonically. Define $U(K)_n=K^{\Delta^n}$, where $(K^A)_r=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathsf{sSet}}(A\times\Delta^r,K)$, and the outer operators are precomposition by maps of standard simplices. A map $D(Z)\to K$ is a compatible family $Z_n\times\Delta^n\to K$ by the quotient universal property; currying gives exactly a map $Z\to U(K)$ of simplicial diagrams. This proves the ordinary adjunction $D\dashv U$ and specifies its unit.

source.place: Example A.2.9.29, coend construction; explicit degreewise co-Yoneda calculation supplied here

proof.text:
Use [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure] for $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ and the Kan model category. The category $\Delta$ has countably many objects and finite Hom sets, so this is a small indexing category. The matching object of $U(K)$ at $n$ is $K^{\partial\Delta^n}$: its data are maps from each proper face, agreeing on intersections, and these glue uniquely to the union of the proper faces, degree by degree. For $n=0$ this is $K^\varnothing=*$. For a Kan fibration $p:K\to L$, the relative matching map is therefore
$$K^{\Delta^n}\longrightarrow L^{\Delta^n}\times_{L^{\partial\Delta^n}}K^{\partial\Delta^n}.$$
The Kan model structure is simplicial for Cartesian enrichment by [lem-coef-simplicial-presheaf-projective-model]. Its simplicial model axiom, in the mapping-space formulation stated in [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization], applied to the monomorphism $\partial\Delta^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$ of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper] and $p$, makes this a fibration, trivial when $p$ is trivial. The relative matching characterization proves that $U$ preserves fibrations and trivial fibrations. By the adjunction in step 1, lifting squares for $D(i)$ against $p$ are precisely lifting squares for $i$ against $U(p)$; the two weak factorization systems therefore show that $D$ preserves cofibrations and trivial cofibrations. Thus $D\dashv U$ is a Quillen adjunction.

source.place: Example A.2.9.29: realization is left Quillen; matching-object verification supplied here

proof.text: For every Kan complex $K$, the collapses $\Delta^n\to\Delta^0$ induce a natural map of simplicial diagrams $c_K:\operatorname{const}K\to U(K)$. Each component is a weak equivalence. Indeed, choose the zeroth vertex $v:\Delta^0\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$. This is a monomorphism and a weak equivalence: the realization of the representable simplex identifies with the affine simplex by $[\alpha,t]\mapsto\alpha_*t$, with inverse $t\mapsto[1_{[n]},t]$; the defining realization relations give both inverse equations. The affine homotopy $(t,s)\mapsto(1-s)t+s e_0$ contracts it onto $v$. Thus $v$ is a trivial cofibration in [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. Apply the simplicial model axiom to $v$ and the fibration $K\to *$. It makes evaluation $K^{\Delta^n}\to K$ a trivial fibration. Its composite with $c_{K,n}$ is the identity, so two-out-of-three makes $c_{K,n}$ a weak equivalence. This calculation includes $n=0$ and $K=\varnothing$; evaluation is then the identity of the empty set. It proves an objectwise weak equivalence $c_K$ natural in Kan $K$, without a choice of vertex natural in $n$.

source.place: Example A.2.9.29: the cosimplicial standard simplex is objectwise weakly equivalent to the point; dual cotensor calculation supplied here

proof.text: Let $\mathcal B$ denote the Reedy model category of bisimplicial sets. By [lem-coef-small-diagram-model-rectification], evaluation identifies $\mathcal B[W_{\mathrm{row}}^{-1}]_\infty$ with $\operatorname{Fun}(N(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}),\mathcal S)$, since its weak equivalences are exactly the rowwise ones; the statement applies to the underlying Kan model category without assuming any projective structure or cofibrancy of $Z$. Its comparison carries the ordinary constant-diagram functor to the coherent one. Here [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization] identifies the localization of simplicial sets with $\mathcal S$. By [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction], step 2 induces $\mathbf LD\dashv\mathbf RU$. By [lem-coef-bisimplicial-diagonal-equivalence], $D$ preserves every rowwise weak equivalence, so the derived left functor agrees with the directly localized diagonal on every $Z$, without imposing Reedy cofibrancy. The right functor on a space represented by a Kan $K$ is represented by $U(K)$. The natural weak equivalence of step 3 identifies it with $\operatorname{const}K$. Hence this adjunction becomes $q\operatorname{diag}\dashv\operatorname{const}$ under rectification, with all mapping spaces and coherent units retained.

source.place: Example A.2.9.31 and Theorem 4.2.4.1 / Proposition 4.2.4.4: passage to coherent diagram categories, using the existing general localization nodes

proof.text:
Spell out the unit so the cocone is fixed. Write $T=D(Z)$ and choose a functorial fibrant replacement $j:T\to RT$ in the Kan model structure. The ordinary adjunction unit followed by $U(j)$ is the map $Z\to U(RT)$ whose $n$th component is adjoint to
$$Z_n\times\Delta^n\longrightarrow D(Z)\xrightarrow{j}RT.$$
After localization, compose this map with the inverse of the diagram equivalence $c_{RT}:\operatorname{const}RT\to U(RT)$ of step 3, and identify $qRT$ with $qT$ using $qj$. This is the coend coherent cocone of the statement; it is generally not a strict cocone $Z_n\to T$. The unit description in [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction] proves it is exactly the unit of the adjunction in step 4. For each space $Y$ that adjunction gives
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal S}(qT,Y)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(N(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}),\mathcal S)}(qZ,\operatorname{const}Y),$$
by composition with this cocone. The dual cone criterion in [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] therefore makes the cocone colimiting. This proves the required equivalence together with its cocone, rather than only an isomorphism in the homotopy category.

source.place: Theorem 4.2.4.1 / Proposition 4.2.4.4; coherent unit and universal cocone check supplied here

proof.text: For a map $Z\to Z'$ all coend structure maps and the bijections of step 1 commute strictly. Choose the same functorial fibrant replacement construction in step 5; $c$ is natural, and its inverse is taken in the localized functor category, so all the resulting transformations and homotopies are natural in $Z$. This proves naturality including cocones. At $n=0$ one has $U(RT)_0=(RT)^{\Delta^0}=RT$ and $c_{RT,0}=1$. Thus evaluation of the cocone at $[0]$ is $q(Z_0\times\Delta^0\to T)$, after cancelling the replacement equivalence $qj$, exactly as required. If all rows are empty, the coend and diagonal are empty and the same adjunction proves the empty apex is the colimit; no nonemptiness or Kan assumption on rows entered any step.
